records.source: Ὀφείλομεν δὲ ἡμεῖς οἱ δυνατοὶ τὰ ἀσθενήματα τῶν ἀδυνάτων βαστάζειν, καὶ μὴ ἑαυτοῖς ἀρέσκειν.
records.gloss: Ought and we the strong the weaknesses of the not-strong to bear, and not ourselves to please.
pieces: Those of us who are strong have a duty to carry the weaknesses of those who lack strength, instead of living to please ourselves.

L.1: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those without strength, and not to please ourselves.

R.1: Some of us have a strong faith. We should help carry the burdens of those whose faith is weak, and not just do what pleases us.

decisions.choice: the strong and the weak: strong and weak in faith, as in chapter 14
alternatives: strong and weak in body or social standing
decisions.reason: The chapter goes on from 14:1, "the one who is weak in faith": believers whose conscience will not let them eat some foods or ignore some special days. Paul counts himself among the strong ("we"), since he is sure no food is unclean in itself (14:14). ἀδύνατος means "without strength", the opposite of δυνατός.

decisions.choice: bear: carry and support, not just put up with
decisions.reason: βαστάζω is to carry a load, as in Galatians 6:2, "carry one another's burdens". The strong are not only to tolerate the scruples of the weak but to take them on themselves, as Christ did (verse 3).

decisions.choice: ought: an obligation, a debt owed
decisions.reason: ὀφείλω is to owe, the same word as in 13:8, "owe no one anything except to love one another". Bearing with the weak is a debt of love, not an optional kindness.

decisions.choice: a strong faith ... whose faith is weak
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of strength is meant, from 14:1, so that a young reader does not think of bodily strength.

records.heading: Bearing with the weak, as Christ did

records.source: ἕκαστος ἡμῶν τῷ πλησίον ἀρεσκέτω εἰς τὸ ἀγαθὸν πρὸς οἰκοδομήν·
records.gloss: Each of us the neighbor let please for the good toward building up;
pieces: Each of us should please our neighbor, aiming at what is good for them and what builds them up.

L.2: Let each of us please [his] neighbor for the good, for building up;

R.2: Each of us should try to please the people around us, doing what is good for them and what helps them grow.

decisions.choice: neighbor: the fellow believer next to us
decisions.reason: πλησίον is "the one near", the neighbor of Leviticus 19:18 (quoted in 13:9). Here, after verse 1, it is above all the weaker believer in the same church, though the command reaches further.

decisions.choice: for the good, for building up: the aim and limit of pleasing others
decisions.reason: The two phrases say why and how far to please a neighbor: for their real good and to strengthen them. This is not pleasing people to win their favor, which Paul rejects (Galatians 1:10).

decisions.choice: building up: strengthening someone's faith and life together
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομή is the building of a house, used for helping one another grow in faith and for strengthening the church, as in 14:19.

decisions.choice: the people around us
decisions.reason: "Neighbor" can suggest only the person next door; Readable says "the people around us".

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐχ ἑαυτῷ ἤρεσεν· ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται· Οἱ ὀνειδισμοὶ τῶν ὀνειδιζόντων σε ἐπέπεσαν ἐπ’ ἐμέ.
records.gloss: Even for the Christ not himself pleased; but just as it has been written: The insults of the insulting you fell on me.
pieces: For even {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} did not please {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. Instead, as it is written, "The insults of those who insult {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have fallen on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.3: For even the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} did not please {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; but just as it is written: "The insults of those insulting {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} fell on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.3: Even {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} did not live to please {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. As Scripture says, "When people insulted {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the insults fell on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 69:10
decisions.reason: Psalm 69 is the prayer of a righteous sufferer: "zeal for your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me." Paul quotes the Greek translation, which matches the Hebrew here. The New Testament often reads this psalm as speaking of Jesus (John 2:17, 15:25, 19:28-29).

decisions.choice: you: God; me: Christ, speaking the psalm
decisions.reason: In the psalm the speaker addresses God. Paul hears Christ speaking it: the hostility people had toward God fell on Christ, and he took it rather than pleasing himself.

decisions.choice: but [it happened] as it is written
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out a verb after "but": Christ did not please himself, but things went with him as Scripture had said. The sense is clear without it.

records.source: ὅσα γὰρ προεγράφη, εἰς τὴν ἡμετέραν διδασκαλίαν ἐγράφη, ἵνα διὰ τῆς ὑπομονῆς καὶ διὰ τῆς παρακλήσεως τῶν γραφῶν τὴν ἐλπίδα ἔχωμεν.
records.gloss: Whatever for was written beforehand, for our instruction was written, so that through the endurance and through the encouragement of the Scriptures the hope we may have.
pieces: Everything that was written in earlier times was written to teach us. It was written so that we might have hope, as we endure and as the Scriptures encourage us.

L.4: For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and through the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.

R.4: Everything that was written in Scripture long ago was written to teach us. As we keep going and as the Scriptures encourage us, we can have hope.

decisions.choice: whatever was written beforehand: the Old Testament Scriptures
decisions.reason: Paul explains why a psalm written long before (verse 3) speaks to the church: the Scriptures of Israel were written with later believers in view, as he says also in 4:23-24 and 1 Corinthians 10:11.

decisions.choice: endurance (ours) and encouragement (from the Scriptures)
alternatives: endurance and encouragement both given by the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Each noun has its own "through". "Of the Scriptures" stands after encouragement, so the Scriptures at least give encouragement; they may also be the source of endurance. Verse 5 names God as the giver of both.

decisions.choice: the hope: the believer's hope of God's coming glory
decisions.reason: The article points to the hope Paul has already described: hope of sharing God's glory (5:2-5), waited for with endurance (8:24-25).

decisions.choice: we might have hope, as we endure and as the Scriptures encourage us
alternatives: through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the two nouns into verbs, which keeps the two "through" phrases distinct in English.

records.source: ὁ δὲ θεὸς τῆς ὑπομονῆς καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως δῴη ὑμῖν τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν ἀλλήλοις κατὰ Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν, ἵνα ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν ἑνὶ στόματι δοξάζητε τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: The and God of the endurance and of the encouragement may he give you the same to think among one another according to Christ Jesus, \v 6 so that with one mind in one mouth you may glorify the God and Father of the Lord of us Jesus Christ.
pieces: May God, who gives endurance and encouragement, grant you to live in harmony with one another, as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus would have you,
so that together, with one voice, you may give glory to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.5: Now may the God of endurance and of encouragement give you to think the same [way] among one another according to {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus,
L.6: so that with one mind [and] with one mouth you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.5: God gives us strength to keep going, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} encourages us. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} help you agree with one another as you follow {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
R.6: Then all of you together, with one voice, will glorify God, the Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: the God of endurance and encouragement: the God who gives them
decisions.reason: The two words repeat verse 4: what the Scriptures give, God gives through them. Paul names God in the same way in verse 13 ("the God of hope") and verse 33 ("the God of peace").

decisions.choice: to think the same among one another: to be of one mind, in harmony
alternatives: to hold the same opinions on every question
decisions.reason: φρονέω is about the outlook and attitude people share, as in 12:16 and Philippians 2:2. Chapter 14 has just allowed believers to differ about food and days; the unity asked for is one of mind and heart, not of every opinion.

decisions.choice: according to Christ Jesus: in the way Christ wills and shows
decisions.reason: κατά means "in keeping with". Christ is the pattern (verse 3, he did not please himself) and the standard for their life together.

decisions.choice: the God and Father of our Lord: one person, God who is Jesus' Father
alternatives: God, and the Father of our Lord
decisions.reason: One article covers both nouns: the God whom they praise is the Father of Jesus Christ. The same phrase is in 2 Corinthians 1:3 and Ephesians 1:3.

decisions.choice: God gives us strength to keep going, and he encourages us. May he help you ...
alternatives: May the God of endurance and encouragement give you ...
decisions.reason: Readable unpacks "the God of endurance and encouragement" into a short sentence of its own before the prayer.

records.source: Διὸ προσλαμβάνεσθε ἀλλήλους, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς προσελάβετο ὑμᾶς, εἰς δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Therefore receive one another, just as also the Christ received you, for glory of the God.
pieces: So welcome one another, just as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has welcomed you, for the glory of God.

L.7: Therefore receive one another, just as the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also received you, for [the] glory of God.

R.7: So accept each other and make each other welcome, just as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} welcomed you. This brings glory to God.

decisions.choice: receive: welcome into fellowship
decisions.reason: προσλαμβάνομαι is the verb of 14:1 and 14:3, "welcome the one who is weak in faith ... for God has welcomed him". It means taking someone in as one of your own, at your table and in your company.

decisions.choice: you
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "you". Some manuscripts read "us", which would include Paul. The sense is the same: Christ's welcome is the pattern. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: for the glory of God: the aim of Christ's welcome and of theirs
alternatives: only the aim of Christ's welcome
decisions.reason: The phrase stands after Christ's welcome but finishes the whole sentence: Christ welcomed them so that God would be glorified, and their welcome of one another has the same aim, as verses 6 and 9 say.

decisions.choice: accept each other and make each other welcome
decisions.reason: Readable uses two plain verbs to say what "receive" means here.

records.heading: The Gentiles glorify God for his mercy

records.source: λέγω γὰρ Χριστὸν διάκονον γεγενῆσθαι περιτομῆς ὑπὲρ ἀληθείας θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ βεβαιῶσαι τὰς ἐπαγγελίας τῶν πατέρων, τὰ δὲ ἔθνη ὑπὲρ ἐλέους δοξάσαι τὸν θεόν· καθὼς γέγραπται· Διὰ τοῦτο ἐξομολογήσομαί σοι ἐν ἔθνεσι, καὶ τῷ ὀνόματί σου ψαλῶ.
records.gloss: I say for Christ a servant to have become of circumcision for the sake of truth of God, for the to confirm the promises of the fathers, \v 9 the and Gentiles for the sake of mercy to glorify the God; just as it has been written: Because of this I will confess to you among Gentiles, and to the name of you I will sing.
pieces: For I tell you that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} became a servant to the circumcised for the sake of God's truth, to make good the promises given to the patriarchs,

and so that the Gentiles might glorify God for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy. As it is written, "That is why I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the Gentiles and sing praises to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."

L.8: For I say that {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} has become a servant of [the] circumcision for the sake of God's truth, in order to confirm the promises of the fathers,
L.9: and [that] the Gentiles [should] glorify God for [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] mercy; just as it is written: "Because of this I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among [the] Gentiles, and I will sing to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."

R.8: Here is what I mean. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} came to serve the Jewish people, to show that God tells the truth and keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word. He made sure that God's promises to their ancestors came true.
R.9: He also came so that people who are not Jews would give glory to God for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercy. As Scripture says, "So I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the nations. I will sing praises to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."

decisions.choice: the circumcision: the Jewish people
decisions.reason: περιτομή stands for the people who bear the sign of the covenant, as in 3:30 and 4:9. Jesus lived and served among Israel (Matthew 15:24).

decisions.choice: God's truth: God's faithfulness to his word
decisions.reason: ἀλήθεια here is God being true: he keeps what he has promised, as in 3:3-7. The next phrase explains it: Christ came to confirm the promises.

decisions.choice: the fathers: the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The promises were made to Abraham and his descendants (4:13, 9:4-5, 11:28), including the promise that the nations would be blessed through him (Genesis 12:3).

decisions.choice: and so that the Gentiles might glorify God: a second purpose of Christ's coming
alternatives: "I say ... that the Gentiles glorify God": a second thing Paul says
decisions.reason: The Greek joins "the Gentiles glorify" loosely to what goes before. It may be a second purpose alongside "to confirm", or a second statement after "I say". Either way, Christ's service brings both Israel's promises and the Gentiles' praise; the Gentiles praise God for mercy, Israel for his faithfulness.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 18:50 (also 2 Samuel 22:50)
decisions.reason: David, the anointed king, praises God among the nations after his victories. In the Hebrew he addresses God by the divine name; the words Paul quotes leave it out. Paul hears the words of the king fulfilled in the Messiah, David's descendant (1:3), so that God is praised among the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews; in the quotation, the nations
decisions.reason: Readable says "people who are not Jews" in Paul's own words and "the nations" in the psalm, where it means the peoples of the world.

decisions.choice: the patriarchs
decisions.reason: "The fathers" could suggest the readers' own fathers; Balanced names the patriarchs, and Readable says "their ancestors".

records.source: καὶ πάλιν λέγει· Εὐφράνθητε, ἔθνη, μετὰ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And again it says: Rejoice, Gentiles, with the people of him.
pieces: And again it says, "Rejoice, you Gentiles, together with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."

L.10: And again it says: "Rejoice, Gentiles, with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."

R.10: Scripture also says, "Be glad, you nations, together with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Deuteronomy 32:43, from the Greek translation
decisions.reason: The words come from the end of the Song of Moses, in the Greek translation, which calls the nations to rejoice with God's people. The Hebrew text is shorter and differs here; Paul follows the Greek.

decisions.choice: it says: Scripture says
decisions.reason: No subject is named; it carries on from "it is written" in verse 9. Scripture speaking and God speaking amount to the same for Paul.

decisions.choice: his people: Israel
decisions.reason: In the Song of Moses God's people is Israel. The Gentiles are called to rejoice alongside Israel, not in its place, as in 11:17-18.

decisions.choice: you nations
decisions.reason: In the quotation Readable says "the nations", the peoples of the world, as in verse 9.

records.source: καὶ πάλιν· Αἰνεῖτε, πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, τὸν κύριον, καὶ ἐπαινεσάτωσαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ λαοί.
records.gloss: And again: Praise, all the Gentiles, the Lord, and let praise him all the peoples.
pieces: And again, "All you Gentiles, praise the Lord; let all the peoples sing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise."

L.11: And again: "Praise the Lord, all the Gentiles, and let all the peoples praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.11: And again, "All you nations, praise the Lord! Let every people praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 117:1
decisions.reason: The shortest psalm calls all nations to praise God for his steadfast love and faithfulness, the two things Paul has named in verses 8-9. In the Hebrew the divine name stands where the Greek has "Lord".

decisions.choice: all the peoples: every nation, not Israel alone
decisions.reason: The plural λαός is parallel to "all the Gentiles": the whole world is called to praise.

decisions.choice: you nations
decisions.reason: In the quotation Readable says "the nations", as in verses 9 and 10.

records.source: καὶ πάλιν Ἠσαΐας λέγει· Ἔσται ἡ ῥίζα τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, καὶ ὁ ἀνιστάμενος ἄρχειν ἐθνῶν· ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.
records.gloss: And again Isaiah says: There will be the root of Jesse, and the one rising to rule Gentiles; on him Gentiles will hope.
pieces: And again Isaiah says, "The root of Jesse will come, the one who rises to rule over the Gentiles; the Gentiles will set their hope on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.12: And again Isaiah says: "There will be the root of Jesse, and the one who rises to rule [the] Gentiles; in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [the] Gentiles will hope."

R.12: Isaiah also says, "A descendant of Jesse will come. He will rise up to rule the nations, and the nations will put their hope in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Isaiah 11:10, from the Greek translation
decisions.reason: Isaiah foretells a king from the family of Jesse, King David's father (Isaiah 11:1). The Hebrew says the root of Jesse will stand as a signal to the peoples and the nations will seek him; the Greek translation, which Paul quotes, says he will rise to rule the nations and they will hope in him.

decisions.choice: the root of Jesse: a descendant of Jesse, the Messiah from David's line
decisions.reason: ῥίζα is a root, and so also the shoot that springs from it (Isaiah 11:1, 53:2; Revelation 5:5, 22:16). Paul opened the letter with Jesus as David's descendant (1:3).

decisions.choice: the one who rises: who comes forward to rule
alternatives: the one raised from the dead
decisions.reason: ἀνίστημι means to rise up or appear, here to take up rule. Paul may also hear in it Jesus' resurrection, since the same verb is used of rising from the dead, but the quotation itself speaks of a king's appearing.

decisions.choice: will hope: will put their hope in him
decisions.reason: The quotation ends on hope, the word that leads into the prayer of verse 13, "the God of hope".

decisions.choice: a descendant of Jesse
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of a root means.

decisions.choice: the nations
decisions.reason: In the quotation Readable says "the nations", as in verses 9-11.

records.source: ὁ δὲ θεὸς τῆς ἐλπίδος πληρώσαι ὑμᾶς πάσης χαρᾶς καὶ εἰρήνης ἐν τῷ πιστεύειν, εἰς τὸ περισσεύειν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐλπίδι ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος ἁγίου.
records.gloss: The and God of the hope may fill you of all joy and peace in the believing, for the to abound you in the hope in power of Spirit Holy.
pieces: May the God of hope fill you with joy and peace of every kind as you believe, so that by the power of the Holy Spirit you overflow with hope.

L.13: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you abound in hope by [the] power of [the] Holy Spirit.

R.13: God gives hope. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fill you completely with joy and peace as you believe. Then, by the power of the Holy Spirit, you will be full to overflowing with hope.

decisions.choice: the God of hope: the God who gives hope and in whom hope rests
decisions.reason: The phrase takes up the last word of verse 12 ("the Gentiles will hope") and the hope of verse 4. As in verse 5, "of" names what God gives.

decisions.choice: in believing: joy and peace come as they go on believing
decisions.reason: The present infinitive describes ongoing trust. Joy and peace are not added to faith from outside; they fill those who keep trusting God.

decisions.choice: so that: the purpose and outcome of the prayer
decisions.reason: The construction with περισσεύω ("to abound, overflow") gives the aim: hope more than enough, which only the Spirit's power can produce (5:5, 8:23-25).

decisions.choice: God gives hope. May he fill you ...
alternatives: May the God of hope fill you ...
decisions.reason: Readable puts the meaning of "the God of hope" in a sentence of its own before the prayer.

records.source: Πέπεισμαι δέ, ἀδελφοί μου, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐγὼ περὶ ὑμῶν, ὅτι καὶ αὐτοὶ μεστοί ἐστε ἀγαθωσύνης, πεπληρωμένοι πάσης γνώσεως, δυνάμενοι καὶ ἀλλήλους νουθετεῖν.
records.gloss: I am persuaded and, brothers of me, also myself I concerning you, that also yourselves full you are of goodness, filled with all knowledge, being able also one another to admonish.
pieces: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I myself am convinced about you: you are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able to counsel one another.

L.14: Now I myself am also convinced about you, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that you yourselves are also full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.

R.14: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I am sure that you are full of goodness. You know a great deal, and you are able to correct and teach one another.

decisions.choice: I myself ... you yourselves: emphatic
decisions.reason: Both pronouns are stressed. Paul himself, who has never met them, is confident of them; they themselves, without his help, are able to teach one another. His bold words (verse 15) are not a sign of distrust.

decisions.choice: knowledge: understanding of God's truth and will
decisions.reason: γνῶσις here is knowledge of the gospel and of how to live by it, enough to guide one another.

decisions.choice: admonish: warn and set right by teaching
decisions.reason: νουθετέω is to put sense into someone's mind: to warn, counsel or correct, as a parent or a friend would (1 Thessalonians 5:14, Colossians 3:16).

decisions.choice: counsel (B); correct and teach (R)
decisions.reason: "Admonish" is rare in everyday English; Balanced says "counsel", and Readable names the two sides of it.

records.heading: Paul's work as a minister to the Gentiles

records.source: τολμηρότερον δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἀπὸ μέρους, ὡς ἐπαναμιμνῄσκων ὑμᾶς, διὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὸ εἶναί με λειτουργὸν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη, ἱερουργοῦντα τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα γένηται ἡ προσφορὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν εὐπρόσδεκτος, ἡγιασμένη ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
records.gloss: More boldly and I wrote to you in part, as reminding you, because of the grace the given to me by the God \v 16 for the to be me a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as priest the gospel of the God, so that may become the offering of the Gentiles acceptable, sanctified in Spirit Holy.
pieces: Yet on some points I have written to you quite boldly, to remind you of them again. I have done so because of the grace God gave me

to be a minister of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus for the Gentiles. I serve the gospel of God like a priest, so that the Gentiles may become an offering that God accepts, made holy by the Holy Spirit.

L.15: But I have written to you rather boldly in part, as reminding you, because of the grace given to me by God
L.16: so that I might be a minister of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus to the Gentiles, serving the gospel of God as a priest, so that the offering of the Gentiles might become acceptable, sanctified by [the] Holy Spirit.

R.15: But in some parts of this letter I have written to you very boldly, to remind you of things you already know. I did this because of the grace God has given me.
R.16: By that grace I serve {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus among people who are not Jews. My work is like a priest's work: I tell them God's good news. Then they can be an offering that God is glad to accept, made holy by the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: in part: on some points, in some parts of the letter
decisions.reason: The phrase ἀπὸ μέρους may limit where Paul wrote boldly (some passages, such as chapters 12-14) or how boldly (to some degree). Both soften the statement; the first suits "I have written" best.

decisions.choice: the grace given to me: Paul's calling as apostle, God's undeserved gift
decisions.reason: As in 1:5 and 12:3, the grace given to Paul is his commission to the Gentiles. It gives him the right to remind a church he did not found.

decisions.choice: minister ... serving as a priest: Paul's work pictured as temple service
decisions.reason: λειτουργός was used of public servants and, in the Greek Old Testament, of priests and Levites; ἱερουργέω means to do the work of a priest. Paul's preaching of the gospel is his priestly duty, and the Gentiles who believe are what he offers to God.

decisions.choice: the offering of the Gentiles: the offering that the Gentiles are
decisions.reason: The Gentiles themselves are offered to God, as Isaiah 66:20 pictures the nations bringing Israel's scattered people as an offering. This fits 12:1, where believers offer their bodies as a living sacrifice. Some read it as the Gentiles' own offering, such as their gift in verses 26-27.

decisions.choice: acceptable, sanctified: fit to be offered to God, made holy by the Spirit
decisions.reason: Gentiles were counted unclean for temple worship. Paul says the Holy Spirit himself has made them holy, so that God accepts them, as Peter says in Acts 15:8-9.

decisions.choice: an offering that God accepts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one who accepts the offering, which "acceptable" leaves implied.

decisions.choice: things you already know; My work is like a priest's work
alternatives: as reminding you; serving the gospel as a priest
decisions.reason: Readable says what reminding implies, and spells out the priestly picture as a comparison.

records.source: ἔχω οὖν τὴν καύχησιν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν·
records.gloss: I have therefore the boasting in Christ Jesus the things toward the God;
pieces: So in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus I have reason to boast of my service to God.

L.17: I have therefore [my] boasting in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus in the things concerning God;

R.17: Because I belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, I can be proud of the work I do for God.

decisions.choice: boasting: proper pride and confidence in what God has done
decisions.reason: καύχησις can be wrong pride (3:27) or rightful confidence. Here it is "in Christ Jesus": Paul boasts of his work only because it is Christ's work through him (verse 18).

decisions.choice: in the things concerning God: in his priestly service to God
decisions.reason: The phrase names the area of his boasting: the service he offers to God (verse 16). The same wording is used of a priest's work in Hebrews 5:1.

decisions.choice: Because I belong to
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in Christ Jesus" as belonging to him, so the reader sees why Paul can be proud.

records.source: οὐ γὰρ τολμήσω τι λαλεῖν ὧν οὐ κατειργάσατο Χριστὸς δι’ ἐμοῦ εἰς ὑπακοὴν ἐθνῶν, λόγῳ καὶ ἔργῳ, ἐν δυνάμει σημείων καὶ τεράτων, ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος· ὥστε με ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ κύκλῳ μέχρι τοῦ Ἰλλυρικοῦ πεπληρωκέναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὕτως δὲ φιλοτιμούμενον εὐαγγελίζεσθαι οὐχ ὅπου ὠνομάσθη Χριστός, ἵνα μὴ ἐπ’ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰκοδομῶ, ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται· Οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ ὄψονται, καὶ οἳ οὐκ ἀκηκόασιν συνήσουσιν.
records.gloss: Not for I will dare anything to speak of which not worked out Christ through me for obedience of Gentiles, by word and deed, \v 19 in power of signs and wonders, in power of Spirit; so that me from Jerusalem and around as far as the Illyricum to have fulfilled the gospel of the Christ, \v 20 thus and being ambitious to preach the gospel not where was named Christ, so that not on another's foundation I may build, \v 21 but just as it has been written: To whom not it was announced about him will see, and who not have heard will understand.
pieces: I will not venture to speak of anything but what {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has done through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience, through what I have said and done,
by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit. So I have completed the preaching of the gospel of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in a wide circle from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum.
My aim has been to preach the gospel where {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was not yet known, so that I would not build on a foundation someone else had laid.
Instead, as it is written, "Those who were never told of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will see, and those who never heard will understand."

L.18: For I will not dare to speak of anything that {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} has not accomplished through me for [the] obedience of [the] Gentiles, by word and deed,
L.19: by [the] power of signs and wonders, by [the] power of [the] Spirit; so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have fully preached the gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.20: and so making it my ambition to preach the gospel not where {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was [already] named, so that I might not build on another's foundation,
L.21: but just as it is written: "Those to whom nothing was announced about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will see, and those who have not heard will understand."

R.18: I will speak only about what {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has done through me to lead people who are not Jews to obey God. This happened through what I said and did,
R.19: through the power of signs and wonders, and through the power of the Spirit. So I have finished telling the good news about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in a wide circle from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum.
R.20: I have always wanted to tell the good news in places where people had never heard of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. I did not want to build on what someone else had started.
R.21: As Scripture says, "Those who were never told about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will see, and those who have never heard will understand."

decisions.choice: anything that Christ has not accomplished through me: only what Christ has done
decisions.reason: The double negative means that Paul will speak only of what Christ himself has done through him, which is why his boasting in verse 17 is "in Christ Jesus".

decisions.choice: obedience of the Gentiles: the obedience that comes from faith
alternatives: obedience to the law of Moses
decisions.reason: ὑπακοή is the response to the gospel that Paul's mission aims at, "the obedience of faith among all the nations" (1:5, 16:26).

decisions.choice: by word and deed: by all he said and did
decisions.reason: The pair covers the whole of his work: preaching, and the acts that went with it, which verse 19 goes on to name.

decisions.choice: by the power of the Spirit
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "Spirit" alone, with few but early witnesses. Many manuscripts read "the Spirit of God" and others "the Holy Spirit". The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: from Jerusalem around to Illyricum: from the east to the west of Paul's mission so far
decisions.reason: Illyricum was a Roman province on the east coast of the Adriatic Sea, north-west of Macedonia. Acts does not record a visit there; Paul may have reached its border when he went through Macedonia (Acts 20:1-2). κύκλῳ means "in a circle", here the arc of his travels.

decisions.choice: fully preached the gospel: completed the first proclaiming in those regions
decisions.reason: πληρόω is to fill or complete. Paul has planted churches in the main cities of the region, from which the gospel can spread; his pioneer work there is done (verse 23).

decisions.choice: named: known and called upon by name
decisions.reason: Where Christ is named, people already know him and confess him as Lord. Paul's aim was to go where that had not yet happened.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Isaiah 52:15, from the Greek translation
decisions.reason: Isaiah says that nations and kings will see and understand what they had never been told about the servant of the Lord, whose suffering follows in Isaiah 53. The Greek translation, which Paul quotes, adds "about him".

decisions.choice: was not yet known (B); had never heard of (R)
decisions.reason: "Named" alone would be unclear in English; Balanced and Readable say what it implies.

decisions.choice: to obey God
alternatives: for the obedience of the Gentiles
decisions.reason: Readable names the one obeyed, from 1:5 and 16:26.

records.source: Διὸ καὶ ἐνεκοπτόμην τὰ πολλὰ τοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς·
records.gloss: Therefore also I was being hindered the many [times] of the to come to you;
pieces: That is why I have so often been prevented from coming to you.

L.22: Therefore I was also hindered many times from coming to you;

R.22: My work in these places is the reason I have so often been kept from coming to you.

decisions.choice: therefore: because of the pioneer work of verses 19-21
decisions.reason: "Therefore" points back to the work just described: the unfinished task in the east kept him from coming. Elsewhere Paul speaks of Satan hindering him (1 Thessalonians 2:18), but here the cause is his own mission.

decisions.choice: many times
decisions.reason: τὰ πολλὰ can mean "often" or "mostly". With the imperfect verb ("I kept being hindered") "many times" fits best, and 1:13 says he had often planned to come.

decisions.choice: My work in these places is the reason
decisions.reason: Readable says what "therefore" refers back to.

records.heading: Paul's plans: Jerusalem, Rome and Spain

records.source: νυνὶ δὲ μηκέτι τόπον ἔχων ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τούτοις, ἐπιποθίαν δὲ ἔχων τοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ ἱκανῶν ἐτῶν, ὡς ἂν πορεύωμαι εἰς τὴν Σπανίαν, ἐλπίζω γὰρ διαπορευόμενος θεάσασθαι ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑφ’ ὑμῶν προπεμφθῆναι ἐκεῖ ἐὰν ὑμῶν πρῶτον ἀπὸ μέρους ἐμπλησθῶ νυνὶ δὲ πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ διακονῶν τοῖς ἁγίοις.
records.gloss: Now and no longer place having in the regions these, longing and having of the to come to you from many years, \v 24 whenever I may go to the Spain, I hope for passing through to see you and by you to be sent on there if of you first in part I may be filled \v 25 now and I am going to Jerusalem serving the saints.
pieces: But now there is no more room for my work in these regions, and for many years I have longed to come to you
when I travel to Spain. I hope to see you as I pass through, and to have you help me on my way there, after I have enjoyed your company for a while.
Right now, though, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve God's holy people.

L.23: But now, no longer having a place in these regions, and having a longing to come to you for many years,
L.24: whenever I go to Spain—for I hope, passing through, to see you and to be sent on there by you, if first I have been filled with you in part—
L.25: but now I am going to Jerusalem, serving the holy ones.

R.23: But now my work in these places is finished. For many years I have wanted to visit you,
R.24: and I plan to do that when I go to Spain. I hope to see you as I pass through. Then, after I have enjoyed being with you for a while, I hope you will help me on my way to Spain.
R.25: But right now I am going to Jerusalem to take help to God's people there.

decisions.choice: a sentence Paul breaks off and does not finish
decisions.reason: Verse 23 opens with two participles, and verse 24 begins "whenever I go to Spain" but turns aside with "for I hope ..." and never returns. Verse 25 starts again with "but now". The context shows the unfinished thought: he will come to them on his way to Spain.

decisions.choice: no longer having a place: no more room for pioneer work in these regions
decisions.reason: τόπος is room or opportunity. After verses 19-20, it means there are no more places in the east where Christ has not been named.

decisions.choice: whenever I go to Spain
alternatives: whenever I go to Spain, I will come to you
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "I will come to you" after "Spain", completing the broken sentence; the earliest manuscripts do not have it, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: to be sent on: to be helped on a journey with supplies and company
decisions.reason: προπέμπω was the custom of equipping a traveler with food, money and companions for the next stage (1 Corinthians 16:6, Titus 3:13). Paul hopes the church in Rome will support his mission to Spain.

decisions.choice: first filled with you in part: after enjoying your company for a while
decisions.reason: To be "filled" with people is to enjoy their company to the full. "In part" (ἀπὸ μέρους, as in verse 15) adds that the visit will be short, or that he cannot have his fill of them.

decisions.choice: serving the holy ones: bringing the gift for the believers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: διακονέω is the word for service of others, here the collection he is taking (verse 26; 2 Corinthians 8:4). The holy ones are God's people, the believers there (1:7).

decisions.choice: completed as separate sentences
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the break with dashes; Balanced and Readable write sentences a reader can follow, without adding to the sense.

decisions.choice: take help to
decisions.reason: Readable says what the service is, as verse 26 explains.

records.source: εὐδόκησαν γὰρ Μακεδονία καὶ Ἀχαΐα κοινωνίαν τινὰ ποιήσασθαι εἰς τοὺς πτωχοὺς τῶν ἁγίων τῶν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ.
records.gloss: Were pleased for Macedonia and Achaia a sharing some to make for the poor of the saints of the in Jerusalem.
pieces: For the churches of Macedonia and Achaia were glad to share what they had with the poor among God's holy people in Jerusalem.

L.26: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make some sharing for the poor of the holy ones in Jerusalem.

R.26: The believers in Macedonia and Achaia were happy to give money to help the poor among God's people in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Macedonia and Achaia: the churches of northern and southern Greece
decisions.reason: These were Roman provinces: Macedonia with Philippi and Thessalonica, Achaia with Corinth. The names stand for the believers there, who gave to the collection (2 Corinthians 8:1-4, 9:2).

decisions.choice: a sharing: a contribution that expresses fellowship
decisions.reason: κοινωνία is fellowship, sharing in common. Here it is a gift of money, but the word keeps the sense that giving expresses a bond (2 Corinthians 9:13).

decisions.choice: the poor among the holy ones: some of the believers, not all
decisions.reason: The genitive picks out a group: the poor who were among the believers in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: were pleased: chose gladly, of their own will
decisions.reason: εὐδοκέω is to think it good and choose it willingly. Paul stresses that the gift was freely given (2 Corinthians 8:3).

decisions.choice: the churches of (B); the believers in (R)
decisions.reason: English does not use a place name for the people in it as freely as Greek; Balanced and Readable name them.

records.source: εὐδόκησαν γάρ, καὶ ὀφειλέται εἰσὶν αὐτῶν· εἰ γὰρ τοῖς πνευματικοῖς αὐτῶν ἐκοινώνησαν τὰ ἔθνη, ὀφείλουσιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς σαρκικοῖς λειτουργῆσαι αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: They were pleased for, and debtors they are of them; if for in the spiritual of them shared the Gentiles, they ought also in the fleshly to serve them.
pieces: They were glad to do it, and they really do owe it to them. If the Gentiles have come to share in their spiritual blessings, they ought also to serve them with material help.

L.27: For they were pleased [to do it], and they are their debtors; for if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual [things], they ought also to serve them in material [things].

R.27: They were happy to do this. But they also owe it to them. The people who are not Jews have shared in the spiritual blessings that came from the Jewish believers. So they should also help them with the things they need to live.

decisions.choice: they were pleased ... and they are debtors: freely given and yet owed
decisions.reason: Paul repeats "they were pleased" from verse 26 and adds that the gift is also a debt. Both are true: a free gift and a fitting return.

decisions.choice: their spiritual things: the blessings of the gospel that came through Israel
decisions.reason: The gospel, the promises and the Messiah came to the Gentiles from the Jewish people and from the church in Jerusalem (9:4-5, 11:17-18).

decisions.choice: material things: what the body needs
decisions.reason: σαρκικός here means belonging to bodily life, such as food and money, not sinful (as in 1 Corinthians 9:11).

decisions.choice: serve: a word for public and priestly service
decisions.reason: λειτουργέω is related to "minister" in verse 16. The gift is a service to God's people, almost an act of worship.

decisions.choice: spiritual blessings ... material help (B); things they need to live (R)
decisions.reason: English needs nouns for the plural adjectives; Readable says plainly what material things are.

decisions.choice: the Jewish believers
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, from the context: the believers in Jerusalem, and through them Israel.

records.source: τοῦτο οὖν ἐπιτελέσας, καὶ σφραγισάμενος αὐτοῖς τὸν καρπὸν τοῦτον, ἀπελεύσομαι δι’ ὑμῶν εἰς Σπανίαν·
records.gloss: This therefore having completed, and having sealed to them the fruit this, I will go away through you into Spain;
pieces: So once I have finished this task and made sure they have received this fruit, I will set out for Spain and visit you on the way.

L.28: So, having completed this and having sealed this fruit to them, I will set out by way of you to Spain;

R.28: When I have finished this job and safely given them this gift, I will leave for Spain and visit you on my way.

decisions.choice: sealed this fruit to them: handed over the gift safely and officially
alternatives: confirmed to them that the gift is the fruit of the Gentiles' faith
decisions.reason: A seal marked goods as genuine and delivered. σφραγίζω here probably means to complete the delivery, securing the gift into their hands; it may also mean to certify it as a true fruit of the Gentiles' faith. The exact sense of the picture is uncertain.

decisions.choice: this fruit: the collection
decisions.reason: καρπός is fruit or harvest: the gift is what the gospel has produced among the Gentiles (compare Philippians 4:17).

decisions.choice: through you: by way of Rome
decisions.reason: Paul will pass through Rome on his journey west, as verse 24 has said.

decisions.choice: safely given them this gift
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the picture in plain words.

records.source: οἶδα δὲ ὅτι ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν πληρώματι εὐλογίας Χριστοῦ ἐλεύσομαι.
records.gloss: I know and that coming to you in fullness of blessing of Christ I will come.
pieces: I know that when I do come to you, I will come with the full blessing of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.29: And I know that when I come to you, I will come in [the] fullness of [the] blessing of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.29: And I know that when I come, I will bring you the full blessing that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gives.

decisions.choice: the fullness of the blessing of Christ: the blessing Christ gives, in full
decisions.reason: Christ is the one who blesses. Paul expects his visit to be full of that blessing, for them and for him (1:11-12).

decisions.choice: the blessing of Christ
alternatives: the blessing of the gospel of Christ
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "of the blessing of the gospel of Christ". The earliest manuscripts and the SBLGNT do not have "of the gospel". Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: I will bring you
decisions.reason: Readable says what coming "in" the blessing means for the readers.

records.source: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ διὰ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ πνεύματος συναγωνίσασθαί μοι ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, ἵνα ῥυσθῶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀπειθούντων ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ ἡ διακονία μου ἡ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ εὐπρόσδεκτος τοῖς ἁγίοις γένηται, ἵνα ἐν χαρᾷ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ συναναπαύσωμαι ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: I urge and you, brothers, through the Lord of us Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in the prayers for me to the God, \v 31 so that I may be rescued from the disobeying in the Judea and the service of me the for Jerusalem acceptable to the saints may become, \v 32 so that in joy having come to you through will of God I may rest together with you.
pieces: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I appeal to you by our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and by the love the Spirit gives: join me in my struggle through your prayers to God for me.
Ask that I may be rescued from those in Judea who refuse to believe, and that God's holy people in Jerusalem will welcome the help I bring them.
Then, if God wills, I can come to you with joy and be refreshed in your company.

L.30: Now I urge you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in [your] prayers to God for me,
L.31: that I may be rescued from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the holy ones,
L.32: so that, coming to you in joy by [the] will of God, I may be refreshed together with you.

R.30: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I beg you, because of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and because of the love that the Spirit gives: pray hard to God for me, as if you were fighting at my side.
R.31: Pray that I will be kept safe from the people in Judea who refuse to believe. And pray that God's people in Jerusalem will be glad to receive the gift I am bringing.
R.32: Then, if God wants it, I will come to you full of joy, and we can rest and be refreshed together.

decisions.choice: through our Lord ... through the love of the Spirit: the grounds of Paul's appeal
decisions.reason: "Through" gives what the appeal rests on, as in 12:1. "The love of the Spirit" is the love the Spirit produces in believers (5:5, Galatians 5:22), which binds them to Paul.

decisions.choice: strive together: struggle alongside, as in a contest
decisions.reason: συναγωνίζομαι comes from the language of athletes and soldiers. Paul asks them to share his struggle by praying earnestly (Colossians 4:12).

decisions.choice: the disobedient: those who refuse to believe the gospel
decisions.reason: ἀπειθέω is to refuse to be persuaded, to disobey. In Romans it describes rejecting the gospel (10:21, 11:30-31). Paul expected danger in Judea, as Acts 21:10-14, 27-36 shows.

decisions.choice: my service for Jerusalem: the collection, which the believers might refuse
decisions.reason: Paul feared that Jewish believers might not accept a gift from Gentile churches, and with it the Gentiles themselves as their brothers and sisters.

decisions.choice: service
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a word meaning "the bringing of a gift" instead of "service". The sense is the same. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the will of God
alternatives: the will of the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "of God", as Paul usually writes (1:10). Some manuscripts read "of Christ Jesus" or "of the Lord Jesus". Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: be refreshed together: rest and be renewed in each other's company
decisions.reason: συναναπαύομαι is to rest with someone, to find refreshment together after hard work, as 1:12 hopes for mutual encouragement.

decisions.choice: pray hard ... as if you were fighting at my side
alternatives: strive together with me in prayers
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of struggling side by side.

decisions.choice: welcome the help I bring them (B); be glad to receive the gift I am bringing (R)
alternatives: that my service may be acceptable
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the service and who receives it.

records.heading: A request for prayer

records.source: ὁ δὲ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν· ἀμήν.
records.gloss: The and God of the peace with all of you; amen.
pieces: May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

L.33: Now the God of peace [be] with you all. Amen.

R.33: May God, who gives peace, be with all of you. Amen.

decisions.choice: a blessing: may the God of peace be with you
alternatives: a statement: the God of peace is with you
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. At the close of a section or letter such a phrase is a wish and a blessing, as in 16:20 and Philippians 4:9.

decisions.choice: the God of peace: the God who gives peace and makes peace
decisions.reason: After his prayers for unity (verses 5-6) and for peace (verse 13), and before a journey he fears (verse 31), Paul names God as the giver of peace.

decisions.choice: Amen, ending chapter 15
decisions.reason: One early manuscript places the closing doxology (16:25-27) after this verse, and the manuscripts disagree about where it stands. The SBLGNT has it at the end of chapter 16. Reviewers must check the apparatus.
